properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 24 at 6:12PM MDT until July 24 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
Excess runoff from heavy rain has ended over the Lee Burn Scar. If
flooding has been observed...Please report it to your local law
enforcement agency. Flooding is no longer expected to pose a threat.
Please continue to heed remaining road closures.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 24 at 6:04PM MDT until July 24 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Jefferson County in central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 604 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. This may cause urban
and small stream flooding. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.

- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Northeastern Lakewood, Arvada, Wheat Ridge, northwestern Golden,
White Ranch Open Space and Edgewater.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 24 at 6:04PM MDT until July 24 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern San Miguel County in southwestern Colorado...
South Central Montrose County in west central Colorado...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 604 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain north of Norwood near Norwood Hill. Between 0.6 and 1.1
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 3
inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Norwood and areas along Highway 145 between Norwood and Norwood
Hill as well as Highway 90 along the Divide Road north of Norwood.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
San Miguel River and Horsefly Creek.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 24 at 5:00PM MDT until July 24 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
counties, Dolores and Montezuma.

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 500 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause arroyo and small stream
flooding. Between 0.4 and 0.7 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Rico and Dunton and areas along Highway 145.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 24 at 3:12PM MDT until July 24 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Gold Mountain burn scar in...
East Central Ouray County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 615 PM MDT.

* At 312 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Gold Mountain Burn Scar. Between 0.5 and 1
inch of rain has fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1
inch in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow
moving through Cow Creek. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Gold
Mountain Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
the Gold Mountain Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of East Central Ouray County

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 24 at 2:37PM MDT until July 24 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows are possible, flooding
caused by excessive rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar
is possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter and Cutler Creek drainages and Highway 550.

* WHEN...Until 630 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and
other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 235 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms in the area. If thunderstorms develop over the
Gold Mountain burn scar, debris flows are likely within
Cutler and Dexter Creek drainages, including Highway 550.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
